tagline: Up the Housatonic, two miles of it kept for fly rods.
intro: From the New Milford line US 7 runs north as a two-lane road through Kent, follows the east side of the Housatonic into Cornwall Bridge, and crosses the river there. From there it goes on through Sharon and Salisbury to the North Canaan line, 28 miles in all.
Two state parks sit right on the highway. One is a waterfall, coming down a side brook across the road from the river. The other is a stretch of the river itself, set aside for fly fishing.

moments.title: Kent Falls State Park
moments.text: Over a replica covered bridge, Falls Brook comes down 250 feet in under a quarter mile, with a steep trail and viewing platforms alongside.

moments.title: Housatonic Meadows State Park
moments.text: Along a two-mile stretch by the park the river is catch and release, fly fishing only, and the Appalachian Trail crosses the park.

moments.title: West Cornwall Covered Bridge
moments.text: A lattice covered bridge of about 1864 carries the Sharon-Goshen Turnpike over the river. The state thought of replacing it in 1968, a local committee objected, and it was raised two feet instead.

sources.label: Connecticut DEEP, Housatonic Meadows State Park
